decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3: “just paste the link and hit Save” and the title is optional. Response entry 6/round 3: “Saving with just the link feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-only, low-friction saving conforms to the save-by-URL requirement.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3 describes an optional manually entered title and a list showing “a title, the link itself, and when you saved it,” without automatic title retrieval. Response entry 6/round 3: “if I leave the title blank, I’d expect the app to automatically pick up the page’s real title rather than just repeat the link.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client replaced the presented manual/fallback-title behavior with the reference-conforming automatic-title behavior.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3 only presents title/link/date information. Response entry 6/round 3 requests “a short description” and “a small site icon” and asks that the saving flow “fill in that page information automatically.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested additional required metadata that was missing from the presented save flow.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 5/round 3: each entry displays “a title, the link itself, and when you saved it.” Response entry 6/round 3: “I’d like to see the title, a short description, tags, and a small site icon.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the original list omitted description, tags, and favicon; the client supplied the readability-first fields required by the reference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 7/round 4: saving fetches “a site icon, a title, and a short description” automatically. Response entry 8/round 4: “Yes, this matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: automatic title, description, and favicon collection conforms for those metadata components.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 7/round 4 enumerates the automatically filled details as “site icon, a title, and a short description,” omitting the required preview image. Response entry 8/round 4 approves the result without mentioning the missing preview image. The omission remains in the exhaustive scope summary at entry 23/round 12 and handover at entry 25/round 13, both of which again enumerate only title, description, and icon.
decisions.note: Prototype review through implementation review: the presented metadata scope excludes preview-image collection, and the client never expresses that difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 7/round 4 says cards lead with “icon + title + description” and reserve a visible tag area. Response entry 8/round 4 confirms the icon, title, description, and tag placement.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: the list exposes all readability-first fields required by the reference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 9/round 5 offers alternatives that differ on existing-tag suggestions: Version A provides suggestions while typing, whereas Version B only describes comma-separated entry. Response entry 10/round 5 selects A because “the suggestions make it easy to reuse existing names.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client selected the reference-conforming autocomplete alternative from options that differed in fulfillment.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 9/round 5 allows adding tags one at a time and removing each with ×. Response entry 10/round 5 says one-at-a-time addition is simple and removal “works as I’d expect.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: repeated one-at-a-time additions support multiple tags, and tags can be edited by removal.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 11/round 6 offers Version A’s general “To read” switch and Version B’s explicit “＋ Reading list,” separate view, and “Done” action. Response entry 12/round 6 selects B and states that links should be added intentionally, shown in a separate view, and removed from that view by Done while remaining saved.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client selected and explicitly specified the reference-conforming opt-in unread state, separate unread list, and mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 13/round 7 defines search over “title, description, tags, and site name,” omitting URL and note. Response entry 14/round 7: “I’d also expect search to look through the full web address and any notes I’ve written.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested the two reference-required full-text fields absent from the presented search scope.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 13/round 7 demonstrates clicking a tag to restrict the list and combining the active tag filter with text search using AND-like narrowing. Response entry 14/round 7: “The search and tag filtering feel natural, especially being able to combine them.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting a tag filters its bookmarks, and the tag filter combines with full-text search as required.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 15/round 8 states that search now covers title, description, tags, “the whole web address, and your notes.” Response entry 16/round 8 confirms searching by title, description, address, tags, or notes.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: the full-text field coverage now includes every field required by REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 15/round 8 provides “＋ Add a note,” Save note, and click-to-edit behavior. Response entry 16/round 8 confirms use of “my own notes” in the completed flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review: bookmark notes can be added and edited.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 15/round 8 says typed notes appear as a highlighted note and can be edited, but does not establish whether Markdown is accepted and rendered. Response entry 16/round 8 discusses note search only and gives no disposition on Markdown rendering; entries 23 and 25 likewise call notes a private reminder without resolving formatting.
decisions.note: Prototype through implementation review: a note feature is presented, but the record cannot establish whether its rendering conforms to the Markdown requirement.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 17/round 9 permits adding a title after metadata retrieval fails and says the description will “simply stay blank.” Response entry 18/round 9: “I’d also like the option to add a description manually.”
decisions.note: Edge-case prototype review: the client requested missing description editing in the presented failed-fetch flow.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 19/round 10 provides permanent removal with a Remove/Cancel confirmation. Response entry 20/round 10 confirms that this is enough protection before permanently removing a link.
decisions.note: Prototype review: permanent bookmark deletion is provided; confirmation is compatible additional protection.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 19/round 10 says re-saving an existing URL does not create a duplicate, reports “you’ve already saved this,” and jumps to the existing bookmark. Response entry 20/round 10 prefers being told and taken to the existing bookmark over creating another copy.
decisions.note: Prototype review: navigating to and highlighting the existing bookmark is functionally equivalent guidance toward the existing item and prevents duplicate creation.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 19/round 10 blocks plain text such as “dinner ideas” with a web-address validation message. Response entry 20/round 10 says blocking plain text with a clear message makes sense.
decisions.note: Prototype review: enforcing the required URL field conforms to save-by-URL behavior.

decisions.evidence: Presentation entry 21/round 11 fixes the collection as a “newest-first scrolling list” and presents search/tag filtering as the way to manage it, without a choice of sort key. Response entry 22/round 11 says it is comfortable with search/tag filtering and “newest-first as the default,” but does not identify or accept the absence of selectable sorting.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented approach lacks sorting by alternative keys. The response is approval of the approach, not an explicit statement of the missing reference behavior and acceptance of that departure.

decisions.evidence: Specification-gate presentation entry 23/round 12 explicitly places “export/backup” in “Noted for later, not now.” Response entry 24/round 12 gives general authorization: “that matches what we agreed. Please go ahead.” Entry 25/round 13 again records export/backup as not built, followed by general acceptance in entry 26.
decisions.note: Specification gate through implementation review: export is explicitly deferred, diverging from the required Netscape HTML export. Neither general approval explicitly surfaces and accepts that reference difference.
